title: The Miracles of Jesus
subtitle: What the Quran and the Gospels report — and what the miracles were meant to prove
summary: The Quran and the New Testament both present Jesus performing extraordinary signs. The Quran repeatedly adds that these miracles happened by God's permission. Biblical prophets and apostles also performed miracles without becoming divine. Jesus's signs therefore support his mission as the Messiah and messenger of God; they point to the One who empowered him.

seo.metaTitle: The Miracles of Jesus in the Quran and the Bible
seo.metaDescription: Why Islam honors Jesus's miracles without deifying him, with Christian explanations and historical evidence considered fairly.

sections.title: Jesus's Miracles Point to God's Power
sections.body: The Quran and the New Testament both present Jesus performing extraordinary signs. The Quran repeatedly adds that these miracles happened by God's permission. Biblical prophets and apostles also performed miracles without becoming divine. Jesus's signs therefore support his mission as the Messiah and messenger of God. They point to the One who empowered him.

sections.title: The Miracle Is Real; the Inference Needs Testing
sections.body:
Islam affirms Jesus's extraordinary signs rather than explaining them away. The question is what those signs establish. God can empower a messenger to do what ordinary human power cannot do; a messenger's miraculous work is not automatically evidence that he shares God's identity.

That argument can be understood without first accepting the Quran. Accepting the Quran's particular account of Jesus requires a further case, introduced in [Why Believe in Revelation?](/articles/why-believe-in-revelation).

sections.title: The Question: Do Miracles Prove Divinity?
sections.body:
The argument is often stated this way: 'Only God can raise the dead. Jesus raised the dead. Therefore Jesus is God.' It depends on whether Jesus acted by his own power or through God's power.

The Quran repeatedly says bi-idhnillah, 'by permission of Allah.' The New Testament describes Jesus's works as miracles 'which God did by him' (Acts 2:22). The Hebrew Bible also describes Moses, Elijah, and Elisha performing wonders, including raising the dead, without calling them divine. The issue is what the signs mean: Jesus's deity or God's endorsement of His messenger.

sections.title: Reports, Belief, and Historical Judgment
sections.body:
The Gospels preserve reports of Jesus healing and performing wonders. A historian can study the reports, their transmission, and what early Christians believed. Whether a particular event was a divine miracle involves further judgments about evidence and God's action.

Muslims affirm the miracles described in the Quran because they accept it as revelation. They should not present that conviction as something historical method alone has established for every reader.

sections.title: The Miracles in the Quran
sections.body:
Quran 3:49 records Jesus healing the blind and the leper, bringing the dead to life, and forming a bird from clay. Each extraordinary act is tied to the words "by Allah's permission." Quran 5:110 repeats the phrase while reminding Jesus that God strengthened him and taught him.

This wording tells readers how to understand the signs. Jesus is God's chosen agent, the power is real, the messenger is honored, and the source is God. The Quran also records Jesus calling Israel to worship "Allah, my Lord and your Lord" (Quran 5:72). His miracles serve that message rather than replacing God with the messenger.

sections.title: The Gospels Also Show Jesus Receiving Power
sections.body:
The selected Gospel accounts include Jesus thanking God before Lazarus is raised (John 11:41-44) and blessing food before feeding a crowd (Matthew 14:19-20). Acts 2:22 describes God working through Jesus. Elisha's raising of a child (2 Kings 4:32-35) shows why raising the dead does not logically identify its human agent as God.

Christians can accept all of this. They believe the incarnate Son genuinely prays and acts in relation to the Father. The biblical parallels therefore defeat the claim that a miracle alone proves deity; they do not by themselves refute the fuller Christian doctrine.

sections.title: Could the Signs Reveal the Divine Son?
sections.body:
The stronger Christian argument concerns the whole pattern: Jesus's authority, the meaning the Gospels give his signs, and especially the resurrection. [John 20:30-31](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/john/20) presents the signs as leading to faith in Jesus as Messiah and Son of God. That is more substantial than counting how many miracles he performed.

Islam answers that real signs can authenticate a messenger without making him the Creator. The Quran states the source of the power repeatedly: God's permission (3:49; 5:110). To decide between these larger readings, a seeker must examine who Jesus is and which revelation speaks reliably about him, not suppose that either prayer or a miracle ends the debate.

sections.title: The Clay Bird and the Limits of an Argument
sections.body:
The Quran includes Jesus speaking from the cradle, forming a bird from clay, and the request for a heavenly table (19:29-30; 3:49; 5:112-115). It does not present him as acting independently of God.

A clay-bird story also occurs in the non-canonical Infancy Gospel of Thomas. The similarity raises a legitimate question about transmission. A parallel alone establishes neither that the event happened nor that the Quran copied a false story. Muslims accept the Quran as confirming and correcting earlier tradition; a reader who has not established its authority should investigate that claim rather than be asked to assume it.

sections.title: Believe the Signs and Worship Their Source
sections.body: Islam neither explains away Jesus's miracles nor turns them into proof that a human is God. It believes them fully and gives glory to their true source. Jesus models this pattern through prayer and dependence on God. His miracles invite trust in him as a messenger and worship of the God who sent him.

sections.title: Follow the Sign to Its Source
sections.body:
The Islamic invitation is to honor Jesus fully without giving him the worship owed to the One who empowered him. A miracle can make a messenger trustworthy precisely because it points beyond his ordinary human ability to God.

Compare the Lazarus account with Quran 5:110, then read [Did Jesus Worship God?](/articles/did-jesus-worship-god). His prayer helps explain the relationship between the messenger and the source of his power.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does the Quran really affirm the miracles of Jesus?
A: Yes. The Quran affirms healing, raising the dead, the clay bird, knowledge given to Jesus, and speech from the cradle (3:49; 5:110; 19:29-30). It also records the disciples' request for a heavenly table and God's response (5:112-115). These are signs given by God, not independent divine powers belonging to Jesus.

Q: Do miracles prove that Jesus is God?
A: A miracle alone does not establish that its human agent is God: Elisha also raised the dead (2 Kings 4:32-35). Christians make a wider case from Jesus's identity and the purpose of the signs, not miracles alone. Islam accepts his genuine signs while attributing their power to God and identifying Jesus as His messenger.

Q: Which miracles appear in the Quran but not in the Bible?
A: Two stand out: Jesus speaking from the cradle as a newborn to defend his mother (Quran 19:29-30), and the clay bird that came alive when he breathed into it (Quran 3:49). The table sent down from heaven (Quran 5:112-115) has no exact biblical parallel, though many readers hear echoes of the Gospel feeding narratives and the Last Supper.

Q: Why does the Quran keep repeating 'by permission of Allah'?
A: In one verse God says 'with My permission' four times (Quran 5:110). The repetition affirms the miracles fully while attributing their power entirely to God — honoring Jesus as a mighty messenger without deifying him.

Q: Didn't the Quran take the clay-bird story from a Christian legend?
A: The parallel with the older, non-canonical Infancy Gospel of Thomas is real and deserves investigation. Similarity alone proves neither borrowing of a false story nor independent confirmation of a true one. Muslims accept the Quran's account on the wider case for its revelation, not because the existence of a parallel proves the miracle.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **The Muslim Jesus: Sayings and Stories in Islamic Literature**. Tarif Khalidi. A Harvard-published collection of how the Islamic tradition remembered and revered Jesus.
- **The Qur'an and the Bible: Text and Commentary**. Gabriel Said Reynolds. An academic, passage-by-passage study of where the Quran and the Bible meet. Including the Jesus material.
- **The Islamic Jesus**. Mustafa Akyol. An accessible Muslim author's account of Jesus in the Quran and his place between the two faiths.
- **How Jesus Became God**. Bart D. Ehrman. A secular historian traces how beliefs about Jesus's divinity developed after his lifetime.
- **Jesus the Jew**. Geza Vermes. A classic historical portrait of Jesus as a Galilean charismatic healer within Jewish tradition.

quranVerses.arabic: وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say], 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِى عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَتِكَ إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ بِرُوحِ ٱلْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًۭا ۖ وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ ۖ وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِى فَتَنفُخُ فِيهَا فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَتُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ عَنكَ إِذْ جِئْتَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: [The Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and [remember] when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from [killing] you when you came to them with clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but obvious magic."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ۖ قَالَ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quranVerses.translation: [And remember] when the disciples said, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven? [Jesus] said," Fear Allah, if you should be believers."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ نُرِيدُ أَن نَّأْكُلَ مِنْهَا وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا وَنَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
quranVerses.translation: They said, "We wish to eat from it and let our hearts be reassured and know that you have been truthful to us and be among its witnesses."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ٱللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَآ أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًۭا لِّأَوَّلِنَا وَءَاخِرِنَا وَءَايَةًۭ مِّنكَ ۖ وَٱرْزُقْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Said Jesus, the son of Mary, "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّى مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنكُمْ فَإِنِّىٓ أُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًۭا لَّآ أُعَذِّبُهُۥٓ أَحَدًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Allah said, "Indeed, I will sent it down to you, but whoever disbelieves afterwards from among you - then indeed will I punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ ۖ قَالُوا۟ كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: مَّا ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُۥ صِدِّيقَةٌۭ ۖ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ ۗ ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ
quranVerses.translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلًۭا مِّن قَبْلِكَ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا وَذُرِّيَّةًۭ ۚ وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأْتِىَ بِـَٔايَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍۢ كِتَابٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: لَقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبَّكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَىٰهُ ٱلنَّارُ ۖ وَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍۢ
quranVerses.translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: “Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,
I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is righteous; because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.

So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me. I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.” When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”

He commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples gave to the multitudes. They all ate, and were filled. They took up twelve baskets full of that which remained left over from the broken pieces.

When Elisha had come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and lying on his bed. He went in therefore, and shut the door on them both, and prayed to Yahweh. He went up, and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself on him; and the child’s flesh grew warm. Then he returned, and walked in the house once back and forth; and went up, and stretched himself out on him. Then the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Most certainly I tell you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father.

So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said,
“Father, I thank you that you listened to me.
I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
